hints.content:
The area of each smaller rectangle is the product of its height and its width.

Once we find the areas of all the smaller rectangles, we can add them up to get an expression for the entire area.

The area of the first rectangle is $2\cdot 5x^2=10x^2$.

[[☃ image 1]]

In a similar way, we find that the areas of the other rectangles are $-4x$ and $6$.

[[☃ image 2]]

The third rectangle has a height of two and a width of three.

The first rectangle has a height of two and a width of five x squared. The area of the first rectangle is ten x squared. The second rectangle has a height of two and a width of negative two x. The area of the second rectangle is negative four x. The third rectangle has a height of two and a width of three. The area of the third rectangle is six.

hints.content:
The area of the entire rectangle is the sum of those areas:

$10x^2-4x+6$
